chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered upon Umm Salma (may Allah be pleased with her), and she brought forward a piece of bread to him. He said: 'Do you have any sauce (idam)?' She said: 'No, O Messenger of Allah, I have nothing except vinegar.' He said (peace be upon him and his family): 'Excellent is the sauce, vinegar; a house is never impoverished if it has vinegar.'

key_terms.أَقْفَرَ: To be impoverished or devoid of wealth
key_terms.إِدَام: Sauce or condiment eaten with bread
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا: May Allah be pleased with her (used for companions)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about vinegar as a sauce and its relation to poverty?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) praises vinegar as an excellent condiment, linking its presence to the prevention of poverty (*ma aqfara baytuhi*). This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on simplicity and contentment, illustrating how staple foods like vinegar sustain household dignity and economic resilience. The praise highlights vinegar not merely as a culinary item but as a symbol of modest living that wards off the hardship of scarcity.
